content.title: Acute management of ventricular arrhythmias and bradyarrhythmias (extracted rows)

recommendations.recommendation: Intravenous beta-blocker and/or amiodarone treatment is recommended for patients with polymorphic VT and/or VF unless contraindicated.
Prompt and complete revascularization is recommended to treat myocardial ischaemia that may be present in patients with recurrent VT and/or VF.
Transvenous catheter pacing termination and/or overdrive pacing should be considered if VT cannot be controlled by repeated electrical cardioversion.
recommendations.notes: Recommendation for pacing when cardioversion fails.

recommendations.recommendation: Radiofrequency catheter ablation at a specialized ablation centre followed by ICD implantation should be considered in patients with recurrent VT, VF, or electrical storm despite complete revascularization and optimal medical therapy.
recommendations.notes: Ablation + subsequent ICD in refractory cases.

recommendations.recommendation: Treatment of recurrent VT with haemodynamic relevance (despite repeated electrical cardioversion) with lidocaine may be considered if beta-blockers, amiodarone, and overdrive stimulation are not effective/applicable.
recommendations.notes: Reference indicated (615) on source image; lidocaine as alternative in refractory hemodynamically relevant VT.

recommendations.recommendation: In patients with recurrent life‑threatening ventricular arrhythmias, sedation or general anaesthesia to reduce sympathetic drive may be considered.
recommendations.notes: Reference indicated (616) on source image; consider sympathetic drive reduction.

recommendations.recommendation: ICD implantation or the temporary use of a wearable cardioverter defibrillator may be considered <40 days after MI in selected patients (incomplete revascularization, pre‑existing LVEF dysfunction, occurrence of arrhythmias >48 h after STEMI onset, polymorphic VT or VF).
recommendations.notes: Selection criteria for early ICD or wearable device after MI highlighted.

recommendations.recommendation: Treatment of asymptomatic and haemodynamically irrelevant ventricular arrhythmias with anti‑arrhythmic drugs is not recommended.
recommendations.notes: Anti‑arrhythmic drugs not recommended for asymptomatic/haemodynamically irrelevant arrhythmias.

recommendations.recommendation: In cases of sinus bradycardia with haemodynamic intolerance or high‑degree AV block without stable escape rhythm: i.v. positive chronotropic medication (adrenaline, vasopressin, and/or atropine) is recommended.
recommendations.notes: Partial row visible on image; positive chronotropic IV meds recommended for unstable bradycardia/AV block.
